questions.stem: A student pushes and pulls a slinky spring along its length, creating areas of compression and rarefaction. What type of wave is produced?

options.text: Transverse wave
Longitudinal wave
Electromagnetic wave
Surface wave

questions.explanation: When a slinky is pushed and pulled along its length, the oscillations are parallel to the direction of wave travel, producing compressions and rarefactions — this is a longitudinal wave. A transverse wave (option A) would be produced by shaking the slinky side to side, with oscillations perpendicular to the wave direction.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a key difference between transverse and longitudinal waves?

options.text: Only transverse waves can transfer energy
Only longitudinal waves can be polarised
Only transverse waves can be polarised
Only longitudinal waves need a medium to travel through

questions.explanation: Only transverse waves can be polarised because their oscillations can be restricted to a single plane. Longitudinal waves cannot be polarised because their oscillations are already in one direction (along the wave). Option A is wrong — both types transfer energy. Option D is wrong — sound (longitudinal) needs a medium, but so do transverse mechanical waves like water waves.

questions.stem: Sound cannot travel through a vacuum but light can. Which explanation is correct?

options.text: Sound is too slow to travel through a vacuum
Sound is a mechanical wave that needs particles to vibrate; light is an electromagnetic wave that does not need a medium
Light has a higher frequency so it can travel through empty space
Sound waves are absorbed by the vacuum

questions.explanation: Sound is a longitudinal mechanical wave — it needs a medium (particles) to create compressions and rarefactions. In a vacuum, there are no particles to vibrate. Light is a transverse electromagnetic wave that consists of oscillating electric and magnetic fields, which do not require a medium. The issue is not about speed (A) or frequency (C), but about the fundamental nature of each wave type.

questions.stem: A longitudinal wave has a frequency of 400 Hz and travels at 340 m/s in air. What is the distance between adjacent compressions?
questions.explanation: The distance between adjacent compressions is one wavelength. Using wavelength = v / f = 340 / 400 = 0.85 m. Option A (136,000) comes from multiplying v x f instead of dividing. Option C (1.18) comes from f / v. Always remember: wavelength = speed / frequency.

questions.stem: Polarised sunglasses reduce glare from reflected light. This works because reflected light from surfaces like water is:

options.text: Longitudinal and the glasses block longitudinal waves
Partially polarised in one plane, and the glasses block that plane
A different colour from normal light
Moving slower than normal light

questions.explanation: Light reflected from flat surfaces like water becomes partially polarised — the oscillations are mostly in one plane (horizontal). Polarised sunglasses contain a filter that blocks this horizontal plane, reducing glare while allowing other light through. This only works because light is a transverse wave. Option A is wrong — light is transverse, not longitudinal.
